obligations.description: Apply the item's discount percentage to the line subtotal
obligations.evidence_rationale: test_line_total_applies_the_item_discount asserts a 10% discount turns 10.0 into 9.0; an implementation that ignored the discount would return 10.0 and fail.

obligations.description: Round the discounted line total to two decimals
obligations.evidence_rationale: Every asserted result (10.0, 3.25, 9.0) is already exact at two decimals, so a mutant that dropped the rounding would still pass. A present, relevant test that kills zero mapped mutants for this rule.

gaps.description: No input produces a value needing rounding, so the two-decimal rule is never exercised; an implementation that omitted round() would pass every test

unrequested_changes.description: The _item() test helper gained a discount key/parameter. The task never asked for the test helper to change, but line_total now reads item['discount'], so without it every pre-existing test raises KeyError. Removing this change breaks the suite, and 'split the fixture update into its own PR' is not coherent advice -- it is in service of the requested change, not separable work.

defects.description: The item's discount percentage is ignored and the line total is quantity times price.
The discount is treated as a fraction rather than a percentage, so a discount of 10 is applied as 1000%.
The discounted line total is returned without rounding to two decimals.
